notes_for_editor: Source is mostly Lighthouse Friends (copyrighted; paraphrased) plus Parks Canada and Marine reports. Conflicts: automation 1980 (LF) vs 1982 (Parks Canada, route des phares); Carré tenure starts 1940 (PC) / 1941 (LF) / 1942 (fr Wikipedia, not cited); Neil Carré ends 1985 (LF) vs 1982 (PC); focal height 25 m (record, LF 82 ft) vs 70 m (fr Wikipedia); tower 14 m both generations. Parks Canada says Bouchards 1894-1940 but LF has Arthur Simard first 1894-95. Access: LF says road/hike by permission; RPCQ says river or air only, operated by Duvetnor; Noreau lease status may be out of date. Marine report year labels are the corpus labels (fiscal years); the Dundas grounding and Batiscan/Bengore Head collision years are not stated in the passages read (Batiscan volume implies 1 Aug 1916 or 1 Aug in fiscal year ended Mar 1917); the 1910 signal station passage says 'arrangements have been made to open'. The 1900 report's lighthouse table (dates 'August 24, 1894') was ambiguous by column and not used. Ship name for Dundas grounding not read. A 1908 list matched by position (Cap au Saumon / Louis Bouchard). Keepers' dwelling rentals mentioned by LF not included. Not found: newspapers, NRHP-equivalent, USCG/Fischer & Bouchard book. Tower height 14 m (46 ft) in LF for both towers.
